title: Alibaba Cloud opens first South American region with two Brazil data centers
subtitle: The company launched its first Brazilian cloud region alongside a suite of ten agentic-AI services, expanding into a market where U.S. hyperscalers have dominated Latin American AI infrastructure.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Alibaba Cloud opened its first cloud region in South America this week, with two data centers in Brazil and an accompanying suite of ten agent-focused services — ACS Agent Sandbox, DAS Agent, Data Agent for Analytics, Meta Agent, DataWorks Data Agent, STAROps, NAPal, Agent Security Center, AI Security Guardrails 2.0, and Agentic SOC. The Brazil region is Alibaba Cloud's 31st region worldwide and its second in Latin America after Mexico, which opened in February 2025. The company reiterated a $53 billion global AI-infrastructure budget covering the current three-year window.

The bundled services matter more than the data-center count. Alibaba is not opening a Brazil region and then adding AI features later — it is launching in-region with agent orchestration, agent security tooling, and a data-agent stack aimed at enterprise workloads that must sit inside Brazilian borders. That is a direct answer to Latin American regulators, particularly under Brazil's LGPD data-protection regime, who have pushed foreign clouds to host both compute and AI services domestically rather than routing data north.

It also lands into an unusually contested market. AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud all have Brazilian regions; each has been building agent tooling on top. The complication for Alibaba is regulatory rather than technical: Brazilian legal analysts have already flagged a potential tension between LGPD and China's National Intelligence Law, which can compel Chinese firms to hand over data. That question will shape which local enterprises adopt the new region and which stick with U.S. hyperscalers.

Takeaway for learners: 'AI infrastructure' is now three things stacked together — physical data centers, model-serving capacity, and agent orchestration. When you evaluate a cloud, do not just compare GPU pricing; look at what agent primitives ship with the region and what the local data-sovereignty rules will do to your architecture. The choice increasingly runs on jurisdiction, not just performance.
